paragraphs.text: Written by him, usque adeo terribili et horrifica oratione, saith Beza, in such terrible terms, as the like is not to be found in Holy Scripture; wherefore it is to be read and used with very great judgment, and not as those miscreants of whom Faber writeth, Quod more magico clam murmurabant hune Psalmum per modum execrationis in eorum hostes, that after a conjuring fashion they muttered out this psalm, by the way of curse upon their enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: A Psalm of David

paragraphs.text: But plead my cause, clear mine innocence.
paragraphs.anchor: Hold not thy peace

paragraphs.text: The object of my praises, or thou that keepest up my credit, as a witness, judge, and avenger of mine integrity.
paragraphs.anchor: O God of my praise

paragraphs.text: There is nothing more easy than to wag a wicked tongue.
paragraphs.anchor: For the mouth of the wicked

paragraphs.text: But with so much impudence as if it were a very truth. Socrates in his Apology, My lords, said he to the judges, I know not how you have been affected with mine accusers’ eloquence, while you heard them speak. For mine own part, I assure you that I, whom it toucheth not, was almost drawn to believe that all they said, though against myself, was true, when they scarce uttered one word of truth.
paragraphs.anchor: They have spoken against me with a lying tongue

paragraphs.text: So that I could not find out any way to clear myself, though never so innocent.
paragraphs.anchor: They compassed me about also, &c.

paragraphs.text: So they smote Jeremiah with the tongue, and our Saviour suffered the opposition of sinners, Heb 12:3
paragraphs.anchor: And fought against me

paragraphs.text: Heb. they satanically hate me. To render evil for evil is brutish, but to render evil for good is devilish.
paragraphs.anchor: For my love they are mine adversaries

paragraphs.text: Heb. But I am prayer, or, a man of prayer, as Psa 120:7, But I am peace. So, being defamed, we pray, 1Co 4:12. When our Saviour was wearied out with the people’s obstinace, he turned himself to God in prayer, Mat 11:26, and prayed for his crucifiers, Luk 23:34 Send me to my toads again (in the dungeon), where I may pray for your lordship’s conversion, said Saunders, the martyr, to Winchester.
paragraphs.anchor: But I give myself to prayer

paragraphs.text: See Psa 109:4.
paragraphs.anchor: And they have rewarded me

paragraphs.text: Flectere naturam gratia nulla potest.

Whose tender mercies may be cruelties; let the devil be his taskmaster. Thus he prayed against Doeg, or Ahithophel, but certainly Judas, Act 1:20. And so the primitive Christians prayed against Julian the apostate, and afterwards against Arius the heretic, whose death was precationis opus non morbi, the effect of prayer, rather than of his disease, saith Socrates, lib. i. cap. 15. We are bound to pray daily, "Thy kingdom come," but must be advised how we pray, as David here doth, against particular persons; his curses here and elsewhere are indefinite, or conditional; either he nameth not the man, or intendeth it if God intend it so; or they are non tam vota quam vaticinia, not so much prayers as prophecies.
paragraphs.anchor: Set thou a wicked man over him

paragraphs.text: And let Satan (or an adversary) stand at his right hand] To withstand him and get the better of him, as Zec 3:1. Or, to aggravate his fault before an unjust judge.
Let him be cast in all his suits, causa excidat.
paragraphs.anchor: When he shall be judged

paragraphs.text: Quot apud iudicem preces adhibebit tot sibi mulctas aecersat, If he beg favour of the judge, let it be the worse for him, as it befell Haman, Est 7:7-8.
paragraphs.anchor: And let his prayer become sin

paragraphs.text: Let his execution be hastened, as Haman’s was. Ahithophel and Judas were their own deathsmen. Doeg, doubtless, came to an ill end; and so did other persecutors. See the Book of Martyrs.
paragraphs.anchor: Let his days be few

paragraphs.text: Praefecturam. Officers are ofttimes the Church’s chief enemies; Popish bishops especially, as here in Queen Mary’s days. Judas was guide to those that took Jesus, Act 1:16; Act 1:20.
paragraphs.anchor: And let another take his office

paragraphs.text: Helpless and shiftless. A sore vexation to many on their death beds, and just enough on graceless persecutors. But happy are they who, when they lie a dying, can say, as Luther did, Domine Deus gratias ago tibi quod volueris me esse pauperem, &c., Lord God, I thank thee for my present poverty, but future hopes. I have not any houses, lands, possessions, money, to leave behind me. Thou hast given me life and children, behold, I return them back to thee, and beseech thee to nourish them, teach them, keep them safe, as hitherto thou hast done me, O thou Father of the fatherless, and judge of widows.
paragraphs.anchor: Let his children be fatherless

paragraphs.text: Let them wandering wander, as Gen 4:12 Cain’s curse. Let them rogue about, - et timida voce rogare cibos. This is many times a token of God’s wrath.
paragraphs.anchor: Let his children be continually vagabonds

paragraphs.text: Or, for that their places are desolate, and will afford them no help.
paragraphs.anchor: Out of their desolate places

paragraphs.text: As it were in nets and snares, that is, in bonds, debts, mortgages; so Chrysostom expoundeth Psa 10:9. Et ipsum et omnes eius facultates inexplicabilibus suis laqueis immites foeneratores irretiant, Let the merciless usurer make a prey of him and his estate.
paragraphs.anchor: Let the extortioner catch all that he hath

paragraphs.text: Who hath no right to it, and will show as little mercy. The Chaldee here hath it, Colligat fiscus omnia quae ipsius sunt. And Quae non capit Christus, rapit fiscus, saith Bernard.
paragraphs.anchor: And let the stranger, &c.

paragraphs.text: Let God in his justice set off all hearts from him that had been so unreasonably merciless. Thus no man opened his mouth to intercede for Haman; Judas was shaken off by the priests, and bid see to himself, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Let there be none to extend mercy to him

paragraphs.text: Pupillis pusillis. Let there be none to plead their pupil’s cause against the griping extortioner, or the stranger that violently invadeth their right.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither let there be any to favour his fatherless

paragraphs.text: Sit eius exitus excidium, so some render it, let his end be destruction; and it is better to take it, as we translate, "Let his posterity," &c. Let them be razed and rooted out of remembrance, they and their whole race.
paragraphs.anchor: Let his posterity be cut Off

paragraphs.text: That they may not live, so much as by fame. The Edomites, Moabites, Ammonites, have no memorial but what they have in the Bible, and that is for no good. And the like may be said of Meroz, Jdg 5:23, which seemeth to have been some city near the place where the battle was fought; but what it was none can determine, since there is no mention elsewhere to be found of it, which seemeth to be an effect of that bitter curse pronounced against it. See Pro 10:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Let their name be blotted out

paragraphs.text: In whose sinful steps he treadeth, be charged upon him.
paragraphs.anchor: Let the iniquity of his fathers, &c.

paragraphs.text: Who bred him no better, but cockered him in wicked courses, and gave him no good example, Partus fere sequitur ventrem.
paragraphs.anchor: And let not the sin of his mother

paragraphs.text: Stand ever upon record in his presence, to provoke him to wrath. A heavy curse indeed.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them be before the Lord

paragraphs.text: Here the prophet beginneth to show why he useth such doleful imprecations against his enemies, viz. not out of a spirit of revenge, or a false zeal, but as truly seeking God’s glory, and his Church’s safety, which could not otherwise be procured, unless these merciless men were devoted to destruction. He remembered not, that is, de industria oblitus est et omisit, he forgot and neglected it on purpose.
paragraphs.anchor: Because that he remembered not to show mercy

paragraphs.text: "The backslidcr in heart shall be filled with his own ways," Pro 14:14. Cursing men are cursed men, as were easy to instance in sundry, as Hacker, hanged in Queen Elizabeth’s reign, and Sir Jervase Elloways, lieutenant of the Tower in King James’s days, according to their own wishes. See Mr. Clark’s Mirror, p. 210, &c. The Jews are still great cursers of Christians, they shut up their daily prayers with Maledic Domine Nazaraeis, and how it cometh home to them who knoweth not, even wrath to the utmost? 1Th 2:16.
paragraphs.anchor: As he loved cursing, &c.

paragraphs.text: Ut vestis commensurata corpori, as the inner garment that sticks closest to the body, and is not done off but with much ado, as he hath wrapped, and trussed up himself in cursing.
paragraphs.anchor: As he clothed himself with cursing like as with his garment

paragraphs.text: Let him have his belly full of it, and his bones full too.
paragraphs.anchor: So let it come into his bowels like water

paragraphs.text: Which easily soaketh through. See Num 5:22.
paragraphs.anchor: And like oil

paragraphs.text: Yet as an inner, but outer garment also, that men may see and say, This is an accursed person; the visible vengeance of God pursueth him.
paragraphs.anchor: Let it be unto him as a garment

paragraphs.text: Opus vel operae precium. The same Hebrew word signifieth work and wages, Actio et merces, Job 7:2 Isa 49:4; persecutors shall be sure of their payment.
paragraphs.anchor: Let this be the reward

paragraphs.text: Fac mecum, sis mihi a latere, stick to me, act on my behalf, and for my benefit.
paragraphs.anchor: But do thou for me

paragraphs.text: As a leper showeth his ulcers to move pity, so doth David his indigency and ailments.
paragraphs.anchor: For I am poor and needy

paragraphs.text: I have my inward troubles also: or I am cordicitus vulneratus, almost dead, animam ago.
paragraphs.anchor: And my heart is wounded

paragraphs.text: Abii, perii, evanui, I vanish, as the long shadows do so soon as the sun setteth.
paragraphs.anchor: I am gone like the shadow

paragraphs.text: Leapeth from hedge to hedge, so do I from place to place, being tossed from post to pillar, αστατουμεν, 1Co 4:11
paragraphs.anchor: As the locust

paragraphs.text: Either for lack of meat or stomach to it; genua labant, my knees buckle under me, the strong men bow themselves, Ecc 12:3.
paragraphs.anchor: My knees are weak through fasting

paragraphs.text: I am lean and low brought. Christ might well cry out, "My leanness, my leanness"; so busy he was for his Father, and so worn out, that they judged him well nigh fifty, when he was not much over thirty, Joh 8:57.
paragraphs.anchor: My flesh faileth of fatness

paragraphs.text: In respect to my leanness.
paragraphs.anchor: I became also a reproach

paragraphs.text: This is threatened as a curse, Deu 28:15-68, but may befall the best, as it did our Saviour, Psa 22:7 Mat 27:39
paragraphs.anchor: They shaked their heads

paragraphs.text: Prayer, like those arrows of deliverance, must be multiplied, as our trouble is lengthened and lieth on.
paragraphs.anchor: Help me, O Lord

paragraphs.text: That I am delivered merely by thy presence and power. It is the ingenuity of the saints, in all their desired or expected mercies, to study God’s ends more than their own.
paragraphs.anchor: That they may know

paragraphs.text: Yea, the rather, as 2Sa 16:12; and I wot well that those whom thou blessest shall be blessed, as Isaac once said of his son Jacob, Gen 27:33.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them curse, but bless thou

paragraphs.text: To plead their own cause, causa excidant.
paragraphs.anchor: When they arise

paragraphs.text: Sicut diploide, saith the Vulgate, as with a doublet, q.d. Let them be doubley ashamed; for which purpose also he here doubleth his prayer.
paragraphs.anchor: As with a mantle

paragraphs.text: Diligenter et impense. God’s blessings are binders; and great deliverances call for suitable praises, the neglect hereof is crimen stellionatus, cousenage.
paragraphs.anchor: I will greatly praise the Lord

paragraphs.text: As a faithful and powerful (παραστατης or υπεραπιστης) champion, and not as Satan standeth at the persecutor’s right hand, Psa 109:6.
paragraphs.anchor: For he shall stand at the right hand

paragraphs.text: Heb. from the judges of his soul, sc. Saul and his courtiers, who judged him worthy of death,
paragraphs.anchor: From those that condemn him
